title: A Comprehensive Comparison of Bovine and Porcine Decellularized Pericardia: New Insights for Surgical Applications
authors: Zouhair S, Sasso ED, Tuladhar SR, Fidalgo C, Vedovelli L, Filippi A, Borile G, Bagno A, Marchesan M, Giorgio R, Gregori D, Wolkers WF, Romanato F, Korossis S, Gerosa G, Iop L. Biomolecules. 2020 Feb;10(3):371. doi: 10.3390/biom10030371.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “, decellularized bovine and porcine pericardia demonstrate possessing the characteristics that are suitable for the creation of novel scaffolds for reconstruction or replacement: differences in water content, thickness and glycosaminoglycans might influence some of their biomechanical properties and, hence, their indication for surgical use” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
